scope: Bounded process-owned byte allocation, full little-endian write/readback, SHA-256 of actual payload bytes, and monotonic elapsed-time observation.

sources.method_retained: A requested resource cannot exceed its explicit allowance. Integer byte accounting and bounded parallel capacity are separate from epistemic judgment.
sources.adaptation: The capsule takes an explicit byte allowance and refuses an incomplete payload instead of silently truncating the model outputs. It does not import the full manager or claim to reserve a proportion of host RAM.

sources.method_retained: n = min(floor(B/C), 4), with no unfunded minimum slot.
sources.adaptation: A pure helper accepts an explicit nonzero per-slot byte cost. Zero affordable slots stays zero; it does not launch an operator or create authority.

block_hash_encoding: Inclusive one-based source lines; normalize line endings to LF; append one LF after the final selected line; encode UTF-8 without BOM; SHA-256.
new_capsule_work: Use try_reserve_exact for at most 65536 logical payload bytes; allocation failure returns an error.
Encode every i64 as eight little-endian bytes, read every value back from the owned allocation, and hash those bytes.
Measure elapsed time with std::time::Instant from allocation through write/readback/hash. Refuse a receipt if the observed time exceeds the supplied budget.
limitations: The allocation is process-owned virtual memory. Logical byte length is not allocator capacity, committed physical RAM, cache residency, or direct DRAM control.
The timer observes elapsed wall time and includes scheduling effects. It is neither CPU-cycle measurement nor a hard real-time preemption mechanism.
The byte ceiling limits the payload, not the complete process working set, receipt strings, allocator metadata, or hashing state.
No physical energy or power is measured. physical_energy_joules is always null; no watts or joules are invented.
The receipt is evidence of the performed bounded computation, not an authority token, authenticity signature, or proof against a malicious host.
Payload identity and readback are deterministic; measured timing is expected to vary between executions.
